title: Normalized completed scalar realization commutes with shifts
statement: Fix a prime l, finite extensions E,L of Q_l and an inclusion $\iota$ : E $\to$ L. Let X be a scheme. Let SE be a coefficient derived-system calculus for E on X [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], $\rho$ a K-injective-normalized Roos realization for L on X, and M a representative-normalized completed scalar realization [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models]. Let c be a coherent shift on the completed scalar cochain functor satisfying its signed coordinate equations, and s its retained derived descent [def-pur-completed-scalar-shift-coordinates]. Give reduction, whole-system scalar change and total limit the independently fixed shifts of [def-sf-integral-comparison-canonical-shifts]. Then M.realization.hom commutes with every integer shift on the entire ambient derived category.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat representative P and a simultaneous quotient-system presentation (C,e,kappa). Compute each total-limit projection on an injective resolution and its shift; in degree j it is the same projection in degree j+m. Transpose the shift equation through the finite scalar adjunction. By the normalized counit projection formula its mate is the reduction evaluation comparison. The universal finite scalar counit identifies the finite representative shift with termwise reindexing. Present P[m] by C[m], conjugating e[m] by the reduction and localization shift isomorphisms. The finite presentation equation follows from that mate equation, and the horizontal equation is the shift of the old equation.

proof.text: Conjugate the old presentation map q[m] by the termwise pullback/scalar and restriction shifts to form q_m. Its unit tensor generator equation is exactly the old equation in degree j+m. The tensor and sheafification universal properties show that these generators determine the chain map. Thus the normalization applied to the shifted presentation gives q_m; all quotient transition maps still commute. Use the system scalar counit shift equation on C without asserting C K-flat. After applying total limit, its composite with the presentation and Roos maps is invertible by the realization normalization and the completed representative comparison; cancellation only uses this composite.

proof.text: Use the comparison formula rho.computes on a K-injective tower and its shifted tower. The canonical limit-to-Roos map has first coordinate equal to the limit tuple and second coordinate zero. The shift (y,x) ↦ ((−1)^m y,x) preserves precisely these two coordinates, so the bridge shift square commutes. Naturality along an injective replacement gives the same equation for the original tower.

proof.text: Use M.normalization on P and P[m] and cancel the presentation and Roos comparisons. The two cochain coordinate equations determine c; the retained descent equation determines s on Q(P). Naturality along a K-flat resolution transports the equation to every derived object.

theorem integralComparisonScalarRealization_commShift
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra ℚ_[l] L] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] L]
    (ι : E →ₐ[ℚ_[l]] L) (X : Scheme.{u})
    (SE : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X)
    (ρ : IntegralComparisonRoosModel l L X)
    (M : IntegralComparisonScalarModel l E L ι X SE ρ)
    (c : (integralScalarComplexFunctor l E L ι X).CommShift ℤ)
    (hc : ∀ P m, completedScalarShiftConeFormula ι X c P m)
    (s : (integralScalarExtensionOfUniverses l E L ι X).CommShift ℤ)
    (hs : completedScalarShiftIntegralNormalization ι X c s) :
    letI := s
    letI := integralComparisonReductionShift l E X SE
    letI := integralComparisonSequenceScalarShift l E L ι X
    letI := integralComparisonLimitShift l L X
    NatTrans.CommShift M.realization.hom ℤ
